newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel urges vote for Germany's largest minority.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel urges vote for Germany's largest minority.

text.p: Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel called for Germany's largest ethnic minority, its two million strong Turkish community, to be given the right to vote in local elections, a German magazine reported on Sunday.
Kinkel's remarks in an interview with the magazine Focus, released ahead of publication on Monday, came days before he was due to visit Turkey to discuss its wish to join the European Union.
"It can not be right that the largest population group of foreign origin is withheld the right to vote in cities and communes," Kinkel said of Turks and Kurds living in Germany.
"For this reason I think citizens from EU-associated countries such as Turkey should be treated equally with EU citizens in Germany," he told Focus.
EU citizens won the right to vote in German local elections through the Maastricht treaty on European integration and were enfranchised as of the beginning of this year.
About 2.1 million Turkish citizens, including Kurds, form just under one third of Germany's total immigrant population.
